findings.text: Ask 5 (the phone shots) has no proof. There are no 360×740 shots of V1, V2 or V3 anywhere: none in this task folder, none in the worktree `C:/Code/lew42/worktrees/replay-bubbles`, and nothing shows they went through `monorepo.lew42.com` with the `Android 10; K` / Chrome/156 UA. The session log says "phone shots read", but `ReciteBubble.test.mjs:525` shoots at 400×860 into a temp `{shots}` folder that nobody keeps. Take the three shots and commit them here, under `shots/`.

The Recite readme still describes the old tap in two places. `audio/Recite/readme.md:16` says a tap on a bubble "plays or pauses whatever Recite is doing right now", and `readme.md:35` says the same about `Recite.Tap`. Both should now say that a tap on a reply bubble plays or pauses that bubble.

`audio/Recite/doc/architecture.md:39` and `:41` still say that resumable bubbles are "the next piece, not this one" and that "tap to hear it" is not true yet. Both are stale now. Add a short decision entry for `Recite.Bubble` covering the ten-word key, `{i, t}` places in localStorage, and replay calling `stop()`.

Replay throws away replies that were waiting to be read. `Recite.js` `replay()` calls `stop()`, which clears `chunks`, `pending_ids` and `pending_updates`, so a reply queued but not yet heard is lost and never marked played. The brief says "stops whatever else is playing; the queue rules stay as they are". Say this in the readme, or keep the replies that were not read yet.

A V1 bubble can hold several merged assistant replies, but `Widget.js` `replay_ctl` keys the bubble by its first ten words, which is only the first reply's key. While a later reply in that bubble is playing, the ▶ does not turn to ⏸, and a tap replays the whole merged bubble instead of pausing.

The comment at `ReciteBubble.js:425` says keys are "refreshed at mount", but `mount()` never updates `keys`. After a V1 `fix` patches a bubble's opening words, `sync()` compares against the stale key until the next tap.

The new CSS classes `.recite-bubble`, `.recite-bubble-ctl`, `.recite-bubble-play` and `.recite-bubble-back` don't use the module's prefix. Every class in `Recite.css` starts with `audio-recite-` (css rules, step 5).

`ReciteBubble` has only static members and keeps no instances, so the class page has nothing live to show. A small instance per mounted bubble would make the bubbles inspectable ("Show the class, and its live instances"). This is low stakes, because the state that matters lives in `Recite.places`.
`audio/Recite/files.jsonl` picked up noise in this diff: a `Recite.js.tmp.49108…` file added and then removed, and a second `failures.jsonl` gone line.

The simpler path holds up. One shared control, mounted once in `ChatV3.reply()` (V2 inherits it) and once in `Widget.Thread.replay_ctl` (V1), satisfies law 6. The `step_back` and `place` unit tests and the fenced headless test cover asks 2 to 4. A fresh agent can continue from this folder, apart from the missing shots.

At 360 px in V2 and V3, the control squeezes the reply text into a narrow column. `.chat-v3-reply` is `display: flex` (`ext/Chat/v3/ChatV3.css:33`), so `.audio-recite-bubble-ctl` becomes a third column beside the text instead of sitting under it, which is what its own comment says (`ReciteBubble.css`, "under an assistant reply"). In `shots/phone-v3.png`, "Your phone's browser is / using an old saved copy of" wraps at about half the bubble's width, with an empty column of about 100 px running down the right. Put the control on its own row (for example `flex-basis: 100%` with the reply wrapping, or mount it after the text box).

`audio/Recite/doc/architecture.md:39` still says per-bubble resume is "the next piece, not this one" and that narrowing to assistant bubbles is "for the per-bubble control the bubble-toolbar piece plans". `:43` still defers the hover affordance to "the bubble-toolbar piece", which the readme's Open list no longer has. The heading at `:41` still reads "'Tap to hear it' is not true yet" while its last sentence says it is now true. The first review's finding 3 was only half applied, so rewrite these three lines to match what was built.

`shots/phone-v1.png` doesn't show V1 where it lives. `ReciteBubble.test.mjs` replaces `/framework/start/`'s body with a hand-built Widget fixture, and the real Start page renders under it. That proves the control mounts, but it isn't the owner's V1 screen, so say so beside the shot.

`Recite.js` `queue()` sets `focus_el = null` whenever a non-replay reply is queued. If a new reply arrives while a replayed bubble is playing, the highlight stops searching that bubble first, and an older bubble that opens with the same words can light up instead.

`ReciteBubble.sync()` runs on every Recite change, including each `timeupdate` (about 4 times a second). Each run does a `querySelectorAll` over every bubble plus one `querySelector` per bubble. That is fine at today's thread sizes, but it is worth an early return when `bubble_state()` hasn't changed.

The first review's finding 8 still holds. `ReciteBubble` is static-only, so its class page has no live instances to show. That is low stakes, because the state lives in `Recite.places` and in localStorage `lew42.recite.places`.
